entries.headline: New Break closes $523,820 flow-through financing for its Timmins-area gold project
entries.dek: The CSE-listed junior issued 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 each to fund drilling at its Moray gold project near Timmins, Ontario.
entries.caption: A drill rig in a boreal forest clearing, representative of the exploration funded by the financing.

sources.title: New Break Closes $523,820 Non-Brokered Flow-Through Financing

unverified_claims: The characterization of continued drilling at the Moray project rests on the company's own description in its release; no technical or assay results were disclosed.
brief: New Break Resources Ltd. has closed a non-brokered private placement of 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 each for gross proceeds of $523,820, the company said. The CSE-listed junior will use the funds for Canadian exploration expenses at its Moray gold project, about 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario.

New Break paid $12,012 in finder's fees and issued 54,600 finder warrants, each exercisable at $0.22 for 24 months. Control person Patricia Quigley purchased 455,000 of the flow-through shares, which the company described as a related-party transaction relying on exemptions under securities rules. The shares carry a hold period expiring March 4, 2027.

The company said the gross proceeds will be renounced to purchasers as flow-through mining expenditures with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The financing remains subject to final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange.
body: New Break Resources Ltd. has closed a non-brokered private placement of 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of $523,820, the company said. The shares qualify as "flow-through shares" under the Income Tax Act, and the proceeds will be used for Canadian exploration expenses, which qualify as flow-through mining expenditures under the same legislation.

The proceeds will fund continued drilling at the company's Moray gold project, located approximately 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, New Break said. The company will renounce the Canadian exploration expenses to the purchasers of the flow-through shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The financing closed November 3, 2026, and remains subject to final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange.

New Break paid $12,012 in finder's fees in connection with the closing and issued 54,600 finder warrants, each exercisable into one common share at a price of $0.22 for a period of 24 months, the company said. The flow-through shares themselves carry no warrants and are subject to a hold period expiring March 4, 2027.

Patricia Quigley, described in the release as a "control person" of the company, purchased 455,000 of the flow-through shares in the offering. New Break said the issuance constitutes a related-party transaction under applicable securities rules, but qualifies for an exemption from the formal valuation and minority-approval requirements because it does not exceed 25 per cent of the company's market capitalization.

entries.headline: Organigram offers $561 million to beat Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis
entries.dek: The $7.80-a-share offer, payable in cash, stock or a mix of both, tops Curaleaf Holdings' hostile US$5 bid by about 21 per cent.
entries.caption: A commercial cannabis cultivation room lit by grow lamps, representative of an industry undergoing consolidation.

sources.title: Organigram launches $561-million takeover offer for Aurora Cannabis
DECIBEL CANNABIS COMPANY INC (TSXV: DB) quote, +0.00% on about $29,059

unverified_claims: The approximately $561 million deal value and the characterization of the offer as a 21-per-cent premium over Curaleaf's bid are figures provided by the companies.
Whether the shareholder vote clears the two-thirds threshold, and whether the transaction completes as structured, has not yet occurred.
brief: Organigram Global Inc. has agreed to acquire Aurora Cannabis Inc. in a transaction the companies valued at approximately $561 million, offering $7.80 per share. Aurora shareholders may elect cash only, 5.86 Organigram shares, or a combination of $3.75 in cash and 3.04 Organigram shares, the companies said.

The offer is a roughly 21-per-cent premium to Curaleaf Holdings' hostile US$5-a-share bid, which Aurora had been fending off for months. Organigram is funding the deal with a $188-million private placement from British American Tobacco and $210 million in ATB Financial loan facilities. A shareholder vote is expected in December.

On the venture boards, the cannabis theme comprises 8 listed venture names; 2 traded today, 0 higher and 1 lower, for a median move of -2.17% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Decibel Cannabis Company Inc. (TSXV: DB) was unchanged at C$1.80, included because its registered name contains "cannabis."
body: Organigram Global Inc. has agreed to acquire Aurora Cannabis Inc. in a transaction the companies valued at approximately $561 million, offering Aurora shareholders $7.80 per share. The offer follows several months in which Aurora had been fending off a hostile takeover attempt from Curaleaf Holdings Inc., based in Stamford, Connecticut, according to the companies.

Aurora shareholders will be able to elect one of three forms of consideration: cash only, 5.86 Organigram shares for each Aurora share, or a combination of $3.75 in cash and 3.04 Organigram shares. Organigram's offer represents a roughly 21-per-cent premium to Curaleaf's latest bid of US$5 a share, the companies said.

The transaction requires approval from at least two-thirds of the votes cast by Aurora shareholders at a special meeting expected to take place in December for the deal to proceed, the companies said.

Organigram is funding the acquisition through a $188-million private placement with British American Tobacco and $210 million in loan facilities from ATB Financial, the companies said. If the deal receives shareholder approval, the combined company would operate five EU-GMP certified facilities.

On the venture boards, the cannabis theme comprises eight listed venture names. Two traded today, none higher and one lower, for a median move of -2.17 per cent against -0.77 per cent for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of -1.40 percentage points between the theme and the broader venture board.

Decibel Cannabis Company Inc. (TSXV: DB) was unchanged at C$1.80, and is included in the theme because its registered name contains "cannabis." The move falls on the same trading day as the Organigram-Aurora announcement; nothing in the day's trading data establishes a connection between the two.

entries.headline: PyroGenesis pays $3.1 million for its Montreal plant after a legal fight
entries.dek: The TSX-listed company had sued the building's owner to enforce its option to buy the Turcot facility before settling the case in May.
entries.caption: The exterior of an industrial manufacturing building, representative of the Montreal facility PyroGenesis has now purchased.

sources.title: PyroGenesis Completes Purchase of its Turcot Manufacturing Facility

unverified_claims: PyroGenesis's stated intentions regarding a sale-leaseback and the planned use of any proceeds are the company's own stated plans and have not yet been executed.
brief: PyroGenesis Inc. has completed its purchase of the Turcot manufacturing facility at 5655 Philippe-Turcot in Montreal, the roughly 40,902-square-foot building that houses the company's operations, PyroGenesis said. The purchase followed a Quebec Superior Court action in which PyroGenesis sought to enforce its contractual option to buy the property.

The building's prior owner had contested PyroGenesis's purchase right, and the parties reached a binding settlement in May 2026 that concluded the litigation. The purchase price was $3.1 million, the company said. PyroGenesis has occupied the facility since September 1, 2012, and plans to remain there under a lease after completing the purchase.

PyroGenesis said it is in discussions with interested parties regarding a sale-leaseback of the property, which management said would help "unlock the building's value" while the company continues operating there and apply proceeds toward projects across its business segments.
body: PyroGenesis Inc. has completed its purchase of the Turcot manufacturing facility, a roughly 40,902-square-foot (3,800-square-metre) property at 5655 Philippe-Turcot in Montreal, Quebec, the company said. PyroGenesis has occupied the building, located about 6.2 kilometres from its downtown Montreal headquarters, since September 1, 2012, and plans to remain there under a lease agreement following completion of the purchase.

The purchase follows a legal dispute in which PyroGenesis filed an action in the Superior Court of Quebec seeking an order requiring the facility's owner to convey title under the company's existing contractual option to purchase, which the owner had contested. The parties reached a binding settlement in May 2026 that concluded the legal proceedings, with PyroGenesis prevailing in its right to acquire the property, the company said.

The purchase price was $3.1 million, PyroGenesis said. The company is now in discussions with interested parties regarding a sale-leaseback of the property, which it said would "unlock the building's value while maintaining operations at this strategic location," and said it intends to pursue the sale-leaseback "at our own pace."

PyroGenesis describes itself as a leader in ultra-high-temperature plasma processes and a technology provider to heavy industry and the defence sector, according to the release. The company said proceeds from any eventual sale-leaseback would help "accelerate projects across its various business segments," without specifying which.

entries.headline: Pantera Silver's shares resume trading after its cease-trade order was lifted
entries.dek: The TSX Venture Exchange reinstated trading Thursday after Pantera filed financial statements and the B.C. Securities Commission revoked the order.
entries.caption: A remote mountain exploration camp, representative of the Bolivian silver district Pantera Silver says is now its focus.

sources.title: Pantera Silver Announces Resumption of Trading on the TSX Venture Exchange

unverified_claims: The characterization of Pantera's renewed focus on the Rakanco Silver District rests on a quote attributed to the company's chief executive.
brief: The TSX Venture Exchange has reinstated trading in Pantera Silver Corp.'s common shares, with trading set to resume at market open on Thursday, November 5, 2026, the company said. Trading had been halted under a cease trade order from the British Columbia Securities Commission.

The commission revoked the cease trade order on October 13, 2026, after Pantera filed its audited annual financial statements for the year ended May 31, 2026, along with the related management's discussion and analysis and CEO and CFO certifications, the company said.
President and chief executive Jay Roberge said, "With our filings complete and trading restored, our focus is back on advancing the Rakanco Silver District in Bolivia."
body: The TSX Venture Exchange has reinstated trading in Pantera Silver Corp.'s common shares after a cease trade order imposed by the British Columbia Securities Commission, the company said. Trading is set to resume at market open on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Pantera's announcement follows news releases the company issued on October 6 and October 20, 2026.

The commission revoked the cease trade order on October 13, 2026, Pantera said, after the company filed its audited annual financial statements for the year ended May 31, 2026, together with the related management's discussion and analysis and the chief executive and chief financial officer certifications.

Jay Roberge, Pantera's president and chief executive, said in the release, "We thank our shareholders for their patience. With our filings complete and trading restored, our focus is back on advancing the Rakanco Silver District in Bolivia."

entries.headline: Washington's China chip curbs put SK Hynix's $45-billion New York plant in doubt
entries.dek: SK Hynix wants to fund the Marcy, New York NAND plants with profits from an expanded China plant Commerce officials have not approved.

unverified_claims: The $45-billion and potential $100-billion investment figures, and the account of the Commerce Department negotiations and the Kessler meeting, rest on unnamed sources cited by Reuters rather than an official company or government statement.
brief: SK Hynix's Solidigm unit wants to build two NAND flash memory plants in Marcy, New York, at a cost of about $45 billion, with total investment potentially reaching $100 billion over time, Reuters reported. The company plans to fund the project using profits from an expanded chipmaking plant in Dalian, China.

The U.S. Commerce Department has not approved the export licences SK Hynix needs to expand the Dalian plant with American-made equipment, and Solidigm executives have met with officials nearly 10 times since late August. Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler has maintained that no additional capacity-expansion equipment will be permitted, Reuters reported.

On the venture boards, the critical-minerals theme comprises 44 listed venture names; 30 traded today, 12 higher and 10 lower, for a median move of +0.00% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. North American Niobium and Critical Minerals Corp. (CSE: NIOB) rose 17.86% to C$0.165, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "niobium."
body: SK Hynix's American subsidiary, Solidigm, plans to invest approximately $45 billion to build two NAND flash memory plants in Marcy, New York, with the long-term investment potentially reaching $100 billion, according to a Reuters report. NAND is a type of flash memory used to store data persistently in devices including data centres. The company intends to fund the U.S. project using profits generated by expanding its existing chipmaking plant in Dalian, China.

Solidigm has requested U.S. export licences for American-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment needed to expand the Dalian facility, but the Commerce Department has not yet approved them, Reuters reported. Solidigm executives have met with Commerce Department officials nearly 10 times since late August, most recently last week. Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler maintained in that meeting that additional American chipmaking tools for capacity expansion or facility upgrades at Dalian cannot be permitted, according to the report.

The report said the Commerce Department has not formally rejected a licence for equipment destined for empty cleanroom space at Dalian, and that separate negotiations are continuing over 2027 equipment-maintenance licences. Leland Miller of the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was quoted saying, "Ultimately, none of this is going to go forward without a green light from the White House."

On the venture boards, the critical-minerals theme comprises 44 listed venture names. Thirty traded today, twelve higher and ten lower, for a median move of +0.00 per cent against -0.77 per cent for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 0.77 percentage points between the theme and the broader venture board.

Five names in the theme moved by more than seven per cent today. North American Niobium and Critical Minerals Corp. (CSE: NIOB) rose 17.86 per cent to C$0.165 and is in the theme because its registered name contains "niobium." Namibia Critical Metals Inc. (TSXV: NMI) fell 12.50 per cent to C$0.105, in the theme for the same reason — its registered name contains "critical." Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE: QESS) rose 10.42 per cent to C$0.265, also because its registered name contains "critical."

Apex Critical Metals Corp. (CSE: APXC) fell 8.26 per cent to C$1.00 and American Tungsten Corp (TSXV: TUNG) rose 7.56 per cent to C$1.28, each included in the theme because its registered name contains "critical" or "tungsten," respectively. The moves fall on the same trading day as the Solidigm report; nothing in the day's trading data establishes a connection between the two.

entries.headline: Novacap-led group buys NATO navigation supplier OSI Maritime, terms undisclosed
entries.dek: The Canadian consortium, which includes Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada, keeps the Burnaby, B.C. defence technology maker in Canadian hands.
entries.caption: An empty ship's bridge at dusk, representative of the navigation technology at the centre of a Canadian defence acquisition.

sources.title: Novacap fund acquires OSI Maritime Systems, keeping NATO provider in Canada
Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE: QESS) quote, +10.42% on about $65,598
KRAKEN ROBOTICS INC (TSXV: PNG) quote, +1.89% on about $2,749,491

unverified_claims: OSI Maritime's claim of serving 27 NATO and allied navies and installation on more than 1,000 vessels rests on the company's own description.
The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed, so the deal's value cannot be independently confirmed.
brief: A consortium led by Montreal's Novacap, including Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada, has acquired OSI Maritime Systems, a Burnaby, B.C. company that builds electronic chart and navigation systems for ships and submarines. The financial terms were not disclosed.

OSI, founded in 1979, serves 27 NATO and allied navies including the Royal Canadian Navy, and its technology has been installed or contracted on more than 1,000 vessels, the company said. The consortium is entirely Canadian apart from one Scandinavian investor, and the deal is Novacap's first through its US$3.8-billion technology fund, which closed in February.

On the venture boards, the defence-and-drones theme comprises 8 listed venture names; 6 traded today, 4 higher and 2 lower, for a median move of +4.07% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE: QESS) rose 10.42% to C$0.265, and Kraken Robotics Inc. (TSXV: PNG) rose 1.89% to C$3.77.
body: A consortium led by Montreal-based private equity firm Novacap, alongside Crown corporations Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada, has acquired OSI Maritime Systems, a Burnaby, B.C. company. OSI builds electronic chart software and navigation systems for ships and submarines. The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.

OSI Maritime Systems was founded in 1979 and serves 27 NATO and allied navies, including the Royal Canadian Navy; its technology has been installed or contracted on more than 1,000 vessels, according to the company. OSI signed a memorandum of understanding with German submarine builder TKMS in June and has completed NATO compliance testing for its electronic chart systems.

The company is also developing what it calls an autonomy centre of excellence to support its work with the Royal Canadian Navy, through which it has previously developed products, OSI said. The buying consortium is entirely Canadian apart from one Scandinavian investor, and the deal is Novacap's first investment through its US$3.8-billion technology fund, which closed in February. David Armstrong, a senior partner at Novacap, and Jim Girard, OSI's president and chief executive, are both named in connection with the transaction.

On the venture boards, the defence-and-drones theme comprises eight listed venture names. Six traded today, four higher and two lower, for a median move of +4.07 per cent against -0.77 per cent for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 4.84 percentage points between the theme and the broader venture board.

Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE: QESS) rose 10.42 per cent to C$0.265 and is in the theme because its registered name contains "defence." Kraken Robotics Inc. (TSXV: PNG) rose 1.89 per cent to C$3.77 and is in the theme because its registered name is Kraken Robotics Inc. The moves fall on the same trading day as the OSI acquisition; nothing in the day's trading data establishes a connection between the two.
